set.reason: The part-whole criterion expressly represents joining by addition; the written two-digit subtraction algorithm is the wrong prerequisite. The scope is operation meaning rather than a required count range. Root checked both endpoint-based reviews; each identifies the stated content or conditional method rather than a curriculum-order claim.
set.scope: The joining meaning of addition in the explicit part-plus-part-equals-total relation

set.reason: The part-whole criterion expressly represents the missing part through subtraction, without needing a column algorithm. The scope is operation meaning rather than every within-ten fact. Root checked both endpoint-based reviews; each identifies the stated content or conditional method rather than a curriculum-order claim.
set.scope: The take-away meaning of subtraction in the explicit total-minus-part relation

set.reason: Here a multiple means several copies of the same amount, and one criterion is writing it with multiplication. That is exactly the repeated equal-addend meaning of multiplication. Specific times-table facts are not needed.
set.scope: expressing several times a quantity by multiplication

set.reason: Both the unit-part and fraction-of-total methods read the given ratio as relative shares. Simplifying to lowest terms is optional, whereas this meaning is common to the methods. set.scope: Understanding the ratio terms as relative part counts before allocating a total
